summary: TypeScript SDK retries too aggressively on 429 (rate limit) leading to extended throttling windows
description:
Issue summary
Customer reports that the Redwood TypeScript SDK is retrying too aggressively when receiving HTTP 429s, causing prolonged throttling and a sustained failure period ("stuck throttled") that lasts longer than expected. Customer indicates their app should back off quickly and respect server guidance, but instead appears to continue hammering.

Impact
- End-user requests degrade from intermittent 429s to near-continuous 429s for ~10–20 minutes.
- Customer sees higher spend and noisy logs due to many retries.
- Their own circuit breaker triggers (they treat repeated 429s as downstream outage).

Customer context
- SDK: redwood-sdk (TypeScript) running in Node 18 on AWS Lambda (concurrency 50–150)
- Workload: chat completions, non-streaming; bursty traffic tied to webhooks
- They recently upgraded from 0.8.x -> 0.9.2 (per customer note)

Observed behavior (customer)
- After first 429, client retries immediately and repeatedly.
- Backoff seems too short and/or not jittered.
- Retry-After header (when present) is not being honored.

Examples provided by customer
Request IDs (from response headers):
- req_01HMY1Q1J5J8ZK2K1ZP4G9JQ2T
- req_01HMY1Q2W9M7R2YVQJ0A1G7K3D
- req_01HMY1Q3H3E0K1NQ7B6F2T9X8C

Log excerpt (sanitized) from customer (timestamps UTC)
2025-01-17T19:22:10.114Z  WARN redwood: request failed status=429 request_id=req_01HMY1Q1J5J8ZK2K1ZP4G9JQ2T
2025-01-17T19:22:10.116Z  INFO redwood: retrying attempt=2 in_ms=100 reason=rate_limited
2025-01-17T19:22:10.219Z  WARN redwood: request failed status=429 request_id=req_01HMY1Q2W9M7R2YVQJ0A1G7K3D
2025-01-17T19:22:10.220Z  INFO redwood: retrying attempt=3 in_ms=100 reason=rate_limited
2025-01-17T19:22:10.322Z  WARN redwood: request failed status=429 request_id=req_01HMY1Q3H3E0K1NQ7B6F2T9X8C
2025-01-17T19:22:10.323Z  INFO redwood: retrying attempt=4 in_ms=100 reason=rate_limited
...
(repeats across many concurrent invocations)

Steps to reproduce (hypothesis)
1) Run TS SDK at high concurrency with default retry settings.
2) Exceed rate limit briefly (429 burst) and observe that client continues to retry quickly across concurrent workers.
3) If Retry-After is absent or ignored, retries amplify load and prolong throttling.

Requested outcome
- TS SDK should respect Retry-After when present.
- Default 429 retry behavior should be conservative and jittered to avoid retry storms.
- Provide explicit config guidance for high-concurrency environments (Lambda) and/or safe defaults.

Notes
This aligns with ongoing cross-SDK parity effort for retry standards (ADR-0137).

2025-01-17 19:41 UTC — Dev Patel (Reporter)
Created from #support escalation. Customer provided request IDs and logs showing ~100ms retry delay on 429, across concurrent Lambda invocations.

Asks:
- Confirm whether SDK honors Retry-After.
- Confirm default max retries for 429.
- Provide safe workaround ASAP.

2025-01-17 20:03 UTC — Owen Phillips (Assignee)
Acknowledged. Asked customer for:
1) TS SDK version, Node runtime, and whether they set any retry config.
2) A full single-request trace showing attempts and timing.
3) Whether they see Retry-After header in 429 responses (can be observed via curl or their logs).

Also pulled gateway logs for sample request IDs.

2025-01-17 21:12 UTC — Owen Phillips
Checked internal gateway logs for req_01HMY1Q1J5J8ZK2K1ZP4G9JQ2T and adjacent requests. Pattern is consistent with a burst hitting per-project rate limits (429). Response included headers:
- x-request-id: req_01HMY1Q1J5J8ZK2K1ZP4G9JQ2T
- retry-after: 2
Customer retries observed within <250ms, suggesting Retry-After not being respected.

Looped in DevEx/SDK eng (Ibrahim Khan / Dana Lo) and SRE (Rafael Mendes) for default retry guidance.

2025-01-17 22:05 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
For 429s, we should be conservative by default. In high concurrency scenarios, naive retries amplify rate limiting and extend the throttle window. Recommended:
- Honor Retry-After if present.
- Exponential backoff with full jitter.
- Add a retry budget (cap total time and attempts).
- Prefer failing fast for 429 when the caller can queue.

If immediate workaround needed: reduce retries to <=2 and increase initial backoff (e.g., 500ms+) with jitter; or disable retries for 429 and let app-level queue handle it.

2025-01-18 00:18 UTC — Dana Lo (TypeScript SDK)
Initial findings:
- Current TS SDK retry middleware retries 429 with a small fixed delay when Retry-After is not parsed (or not wired through in the fetch implementation).
- In Node, we may be losing header access depending on runtime (undici vs global fetch) and how we normalize headers.

Action:
- Patch to properly read Retry-After and apply it.
- Adjust defaults per ADR-0137 draft (max attempts lower; backoff/jitter; retry budget).

Tracking in ENG-2487; will reference TS PR once up.

2025-01-18 01:02 UTC — Owen Phillips
Provided customer workaround guidance (temporary):
- Set max retries to 0–2 for 429s.
- Add client-side queueing/backpressure for burst traffic.
- If using Lambda, avoid all invocations retrying simultaneously; use jitter.

Requested customer confirm they can apply a retry configuration override in their current version and share config snippet.

2025-01-18 16:27 UTC — Customer (NarrativeIQ) via Support
Confirmed:
- Using redwood-sdk@0.9.2
- Node 18.x Lambda
- No custom retry config set
- They do see Retry-After: 2 on 429 responses (captured via a proxy)

They can temporarily set retries to 0, but they want a default that won’t create a retry storm because they have other services using Python SDK that behaves more conservatively.

2025-01-20 18:44 UTC — Owen Phillips
Internal reproduction:
- Using TS SDK 0.9.2, simulated 429 with Retry-After=2.
- Observed retry loop does not sleep for 2s; uses default short delay.
- Confirms issue: Retry-After header not being honored; plus default delay too aggressive.

Next steps:
- Wait on DevEx patch; coordinate release notes and customer comms.
- Suggest customer set retries to 0 for 429 immediately (fail fast) and rely on queue/retry at job layer with backoff.

2025-01-24 21:10 UTC — Dana Lo
TS fix is up and under review: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-287.json
Changes:
- Properly parse Retry-After (seconds + HTTP date forms).
- Exponential backoff + jitter for retryable errors.
- Lower default max attempts to reduce amplification.
- Add explicit hooks/config for retry classifier and per-request overrides.

Also coordinating with platform on consistent Retry-After behavior + structured 429 payloads (PRs 18342/18343).

2025-01-28 17:05 UTC — Owen Phillips
Customer offered to test prerelease. Shared prerelease tag and asked them to run a controlled burst test.

Also shared guidance:
- Use a single shared client instance (avoid per-invocation client instantiation).
- Cap concurrency and add queueing for bursty webhook processing.
- Log x-request-id and retry decision (attempt, delay, reason) but do not log API keys.

2025-02-02 20:49 UTC — Customer (NarrativeIQ) via Support
Tested the prerelease build:
- Retries now wait ~2 seconds when Retry-After present.
- With jitter/backoff, the system recovers quickly instead of extending the throttle window.
- Observed fewer total requests during throttle and less noise.

They request confirmation of GA release version and whether this change is default behavior (no config needed).

2025-02-03 18:12 UTC — Owen Phillips
Confirmed fix will ship as part of next TS SDK release (0.10.x) with updated defaults per cross-SDK standardization. Customer confirmed workaround removed; leaving default behavior.

Marking Resolved. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-2482/ENG-2487 and docs updates.
resolution:
Resolved via TypeScript SDK retry policy updates:
- Honor Retry-After on 429 responses.
- Replace aggressive fixed-delay retries with exponential backoff + jitter and tighter default retry limits.
- Add configurable retry classifier/hooks to let customers tune behavior for high-concurrency environments.

Customer validated prerelease behavior and confirmed reduced throttling duration and request amplification.

References:
- TS SDK fix: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-287.json
- Platform header/payload consistency improvements: sources/github/redwood/pr-18342.json, sources/github/redwood/pr-18343.json
